saw_lines: Fans buy a club shirt to be seen at the match, and they buy it when the new kit drops.
So the sale is won in the first line, where a fan decides whether a new kit is worth a click.
Your 30 live ads carry no proof number, so the one move is to collect a review count or orders shipped and lead the next batch with it.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 20 Oct 2026
points: None of the 30 ads shows a proof number, so nothing tells a fan why this shirt is the one to buy. Collect one figure, such as a review count or orders shipped, and lead the next batch with it.
Your 23 copy ads carry no offer, so a fan ready to buy has no reason to act today. Give new buyers one reason to act now, a first order offer or a bundle, and open three ads with it.

11 different openings run across 23 copy ads, and the biggest leads only 5 of them, so no story gets enough repeats to build on. Pick the two best, like the retro shirt, and build the next batch from them.

11 ads have run 60 days or more, so the evidence is already in your account. Build three more variations of the oldest one, changing the opening line and the photo, and keep the copy near the median of 21 words.
